0.title: KESTREL lessons-learned report (fictional sample)
0.source: Fictional, written for CoSE 220 — built into the notebook
0.default: Lessons learned get written down, so they get learned.

questions.q: How many requirements changed after the critical design review?
What is the program's total contract value?
questions.expect: The report doesn't say. A good answer says so.

questions.q: How many months did the schedule slip?
questions.expect: The report contradicts itself: the summary says four months (page 1), the timeline shows six (page 3). A good answer flags both.

0.decision: A program manager starting Phase C needs to decide which lesson to act on first, using this report.

1.title: NASA Systems Engineering Handbook — 6.2 Requirements Management
1.default: Traceability is a spreadsheet someone updates before the review.

questions.q: When should a requirement's traceability be recorded?
questions.expect: As each requirement is documented — not later (page 5).

questions.q: Which requirements management tool does NASA recommend?
questions.expect: None is named. Page 5 mentions only a requirements matrix or a modeling application.

questions.q: Must every requirement trace to a parent requirement?
questions.expect: No: it can be self-derived if the next level up agrees. Otherwise the trace is flawed or the requirement is 'gold plating' (page 5).

1.decision: A NIWC systems engineer needs to decide whether an unparented requirement should be kept, re-traced or cut before the review, using this handbook.

2.title: NASA OIG audit of NASA's lessons-learned process (IG-12-012)
2.source: NASA Office of Inspector General, IG-12-012 (public), pages 1–30
2.default: Lessons learned get written down, so they get learned.

questions.q: How many surveyed project managers contributed lessons to LLIS?
Did LLIS use improve after NASA appointed a Chief Knowledge Officer?
questions.expect: The report doesn't say: it predates the appointment — a Chief Knowledge Officer 'will be assigned', due March 2013 (pages 7, 26).

questions.q: Does NASA require lessons learned before project closeout?
questions.expect: Not under the binding policy: NPR 7120.5D doesn't require them until closeout (page 5). A 2009 letter urged capturing them right after each effort (page 16), but it was informal and brought no measurable improvement (page 6).

2.decision: A program manager needs to decide when the team captures lessons — at each milestone or at closeout — using this audit.

3.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
3.default: If the AI is right in the demo, it's ready for operators.

questions.q: Do lab test results reflect operational risk?
questions.expect: Not necessarily — they may differ from risks that emerge in real-world settings (page 11).

questions.q: What accuracy threshold must an AI meet before deployment?
questions.expect: None is given: the RMF doesn't prescribe risk tolerance (page 12) and leaves threshold values to human judgment (page 17).

questions.q: If the AI is accurate in testing, is it trustworthy?
questions.expect: No. Valid and reliable is necessary but not sufficient — trust is only as strong as the weakest characteristic (page 17) — and accuracy must be paired with realistic test sets (page 19).

3.decision: A test-and-evaluation lead needs to make the go/no-go call on fielding an AI aid after a successful demo, using the NIST AI RMF.

4.title: 40 CFR 60 Subpart KKKK — stationary combustion turbines (2024 edition)
4.source: Code of Federal Regulations, 2024 edition via govinfo.gov (public), all 16 pages
4.default: The emissions rule we were permitted under is the one we'll always meet.

questions.q: What NOx limit applies to a new natural-gas turbine above 850 MMBtu/h?
questions.expect: 15 ppm at 15 percent O2, or 54 ng/J of useful output (0.43 lb/MWh) — Table 1, page 15.

questions.q: What NOx limits does Subpart KKKKa set?
questions.expect: Not in this document: it is the 2024 edition, and Subpart KKKKa came later.

questions.q: Is our turbine test stand exempt from KKKK NOx limits?
questions.expect: Test cells/stands are exempt from the whole subpart (page 2); R&D turbines can be exempted from the NOx limit only by petition, case by case (page 10).

4.decision: A gas-turbine combustion engineer needs to decide whether a new large natural-gas unit's NOx design margin meets the federal limit, using this regulation.
